47A reminded me of the clue in the Mini [Rarities in baseball routs], which solves to OUTS.  While I understand that the conceit in the Mini is that all the answers had to rhyme with the last words of the clues, there are just as many OUTS in a rout as in a close game...barring unusual circumstances like extra innings and rain-shortened games.  Every losing team gets 27 outs, every winning team also gets 27 outs, but if they're the home team, they don't have to bat in the ninth innnings, so they only make 24 outs.  

The margin of victory (or defeat) doesn't matter.  The currency of most other sports is the clock; that of baseball is outs...if you don't spend your 27 outs, you can never lose.  

BTW, an even better clue for 47A would have been [Make out...or make it].

"Come to Elfland," the troll said.

"N-no," said the child.

"Why not?" said the troll.

"Mother made a jam roll this morning," said the child. And she walked on gravely home. Had it not been for that chance jam roll she had gone to Elfland.

"Jam!" said the troll contemptuously and thought of the tarns of
Elfland, the great lily-leaves lying flat upon their solemn waters, the huge blue lilies towering into the elf-light above the green deep tarns: for jam this child had forsaken them!
